about.description:
MUMPS (MUltifrontal Massively Parallel Solver) is a package for solving
systems of linear equations of the form Ax = b, where A is a square sparse
matrix that can be either unsymmetric, symmetric positive definite, or
general symmetric, on distributed memory computers. MUMPS implements a
direct method based on a multifrontal approach which performs a Gaussian
factorization.
about.summary: MUMPS: a parallel sparse direct solver

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "5.8.2"
  build_num: 3

recipe:
  name: mumps
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://mumps-solver.org/MUMPS_${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: eb515aa688e6dbab414bb6e889ff4c8b23f1691a843c68da5230a33ac4db7039
  patches:
    - flang-support.patch
    - ifdef-openmp.patch

build:
  number: ${{ build_num }}

outputs:
  - package:
      name: mumps-include
    build:
      skip: win
      script: build-headers
      variant:
        use_keys:
          - mpi
          - scotch_intsize
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          include:
            - mumps_compat.h
            - mumps_int_def.h
            - smumps_c.h
            - smumps_struc.h
            - dmumps_c.h
            - dmumps_struc.h
            - cmumps_c.h
            - cmumps_struc.h
            - zmumps_c.h
            - zmumps_struc.h
  - package:
      name: mumps-seq
    build:
      skip: mpi != 'nompi'
      script: build-mumps
      # Tag the Fortran ABI into the build string so the flang and ifx variants
      # on Windows are distinguishable and pinnable. See module_abi in
      # conda_build_config.yaml.
      string: ${{ module_abi }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_num }}
      # Keep flang the default on Windows. The ifx variant carries the same
      # name/version/build-number as the flang one, so without this the solver
      # could hand an ifx build to an existing consumer that never asked for it.
      # down_prioritize_variant is implemented via track_features, so the ifx
      # build is only ever selected when something explicitly requests it
      # (e.g. `mumps-seq-fortran-devel * ifx_*`).
      variant:
        down_prioritize_variant: ${{ 1 if module_abi == 'ifx' else 0 }}
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('fortran') }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - if: win
          then:
            - cmake
            - ninja
            - m2-patch
          else:
            - make
        - if: osx
          then: llvm-openmp
        - if: linux
          then:
            - libgomp
            - patchelf
        # python version specified to avoid windows build matrix
        # not sure why that happens
        - python 3.11.*
        - if: mpi == 'openmpi' and build_platform != target_platform
          then: ${{ mpi }}
      host:
        - libblas
        - liblapack
        - if: not win
          then:
            - metis
            - libscotch
            - libscotch * int${{ scotch_intsize }}_*
        # flang needs LLVM OpenMP runtime; ifx needs MKL headers/libs
        - if: win and fortran_compiler == 'flang'
          then:
            - llvm-openmp
            - llvm-openmp-fortran ${{ fortran_compiler_version }}.*
        - if: win and fortran_compiler == 'ifx'
          then:
            - mkl-devel
      run:
        - if: not win
          then:
            - ${{ pin_subpackage('mumps-include', exact=True) }}
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mumps-seq', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
      run_constraints:
        - libopenblas * *openmp*
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          files:
            - if: win
              then:
                - Library/lib/mumps_common.lib
                - Library/lib/pord.lib
              else:
                - lib/pkgconfig/smumps_seq.pc
                - lib/pkgconfig/dmumps_seq.pc
                - lib/pkgconfig/cmumps_seq.pc
                - lib/pkgconfig/zmumps_seq.pc
          lib:
            - if: win
              then:
                - smumps
                - dmumps
                - cmumps
                - zmumps
              else:
                - mpiseq
                - mpiseq_seq
                - mumps_common_seq
                - pord_seq
                - smumps_seq
                - dmumps_seq
                - cmumps_seq
                - zmumps_seq
          include:
            - if: win
              then:
                - mumps_compat.h
                - mumps_int_def.h
                - smumps_c.h
                - smumps_struc.h
                - dmumps_c.h
                - dmumps_struc.h
                - cmumps_c.h
                - cmumps_struc.h
                - zmumps_c.h
                - zmumps_struc.h
                - mumps_seq/mpi.h
                - mumps_seq/mpif.h
      # On Windows build-mumps.bat rewrites the installed Fortran headers with
      # make_integers_explicit.py. CMake compiles the bundled simpletests
      # *before* that rewrite and only runs them afterwards, so nothing
      # actually compiles the patched headers. This does, and asserts the
      # property the rewrite exists to guarantee: the derived-type layout must
      # not change when a consumer compiles with a 64-bit default INTEGER.
      - if: win
        then:
          script:
            - python test-header-abi.py
          files:
            recipe:
              - test-header-abi.py
              - test_header_abi.f90
          requirements:
            run:
              - ${{ compiler('c') }}
              - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
              - ${{ compiler('fortran') }}
              - python
      - if: not win
        then:
          script: run_test-seq
          files:
            source:
              - examples/
          requirements:
            run:
              - ${{ compiler("c") }}
              - ${{ compiler("fortran") }}
              - make
              - pkg-config

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Fortran ABI marker packages.
  #
  # MUMPS' C interface (dmumps_c.h) is ABI stable across Fortran compilers, but
  # its Fortran interface is not: symbol mangling, derived-type layout and the
  # Fortran runtime all depend on the compiler that built the libraries. On
  # Windows we ship both a flang and an ifx build, so a Fortran consumer has to
  # be able to say which one it needs.
  #
  # `mumps-*-fortran-devel` is a metapackage that does exactly that. Depend on it from
  # `host:` as e.g.
  #
  #     - mumps-seq-fortran-devel * ${{ module_abi }}_*
  #
  # and the ABI-matched `mumps-seq` is pulled into both host and (via the
  # run-export below) run. Consumers of the C interface should keep depending on
  # plain `mumps-seq` / `mumps-mpi` and stay unconstrained.
  #
  # See https://github.com/conda-forge/flang-activation-feedstock/issues/14
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - package:
      name: mumps-seq-fortran-devel
    build:
      skip: mpi != 'nompi'
      string: ${{ module_abi }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_num }}
      variant:
        # scotch_intsize is irrelevant to the ABI marker itself, but keeping it
        # here mirrors the variant matrix of the package being pinned and keeps
        # conda-smithy splitting CI jobs per intsize as before.
        use_keys:
          - module_abi
          - mpi
          - scotch_intsize
        # see note on mumps-seq above
        down_prioritize_variant: ${{ 1 if module_abi == 'ifx' else 0 }}
    requirements:
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mumps-seq', upper_bound='x.x.x', build=module_abi ~ '_*') }}
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mumps-seq', upper_bound='x.x.x', build=module_abi ~ '_*') }}
    tests:
      - script:
          - python test-fortran-abi.py mumps-seq ${{ module_abi }}
        files:
          recipe:
            - test-fortran-abi.py
        requirements:
          run:
            - python

    about:
      summary: Fortran ABI marker for mumps-seq
      description: |
        Fortran ABI marker for `mumps-seq`. Depend on this only if you call MUMPS
        from Fortran.

        The C interface (`dmumps_c.h`) is ABI stable across compilers, so C and
        C++ consumers should depend on `mumps-seq` directly and ignore this
        package.

        The Fortran interface is not: symbol mangling, derived-type layout and
        the Fortran runtime all depend on the compiler that built the library,
        and on Windows both a flang and an Intel ifx build are published.
        Fortran consumers should put the matching ABI in `host:`:

            - mumps-seq-fortran-devel * flang_*

        The build-string prefix names the ABI: `flang_` or `ifx_` on Windows
        (`flang_` is the conda-forge default), `gfortran_` elsewhere. Depending
        on it run-exports a matching pin, so the ABI you build against is the
        one installed at runtime.

        Nothing enforces this automatically -- pick the prefix matching the
        compiler your recipe builds with. A mismatch still links, and fails at
        runtime.
  - package:
      name: mumps-mpi
    build:
      skip: mpi == 'nompi'
      script: build-mumps
      string: ${{ module_abi }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_num }}
      # Keep flang the default on Windows. The ifx variant carries the same
      # name/version/build-number as the flang one, so without this the solver
      # could hand an ifx build to an existing consumer that never asked for it.
      # down_prioritize_variant is implemented via track_features, so the ifx
      # build is only ever selected when something explicitly requests it
      # (e.g. `mumps-seq-fortran-devel * ifx_*`).
      variant:
        down_prioritize_variant: ${{ 1 if module_abi == 'ifx' else 0 }}
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('fortran') }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - make
        - if: osx
          then:
            - llvm-openmp
        - if: linux
          then:
            - libgomp
            - patchelf
        - if: "mpi == 'openmpi' and build_platform != target_platform"
          then: ${{ mpi }}
        - python 3.11.*
      host:
        - libblas
        - liblapack
        - ${{ mpi }}
        - metis
        - parmetis
        - libptscotch
        - libscotch * int${{ scotch_intsize }}_*
        - scalapack
        - libscotch
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mumps-include', exact=True) }}
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mumps-mpi', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
      run_constraints:
        - libopenblas * *openmp*
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          files:
            - lib/pkgconfig/smumps.pc
            - lib/pkgconfig/dmumps.pc
            - lib/pkgconfig/cmumps.pc
            - lib/pkgconfig/zmumps.pc
          lib:
            - mumps_common
            - pord
            - smumps
            - dmumps
            - cmumps
            - zmumps
      - script:
          file: run_test-mpi
        files:
          source:
            - examples/
        requirements:
          run:
            - ${{ compiler("c") }}
            - ${{ compiler("fortran") }}
            - make
            - pkg-config

  - package:
      name: mumps-mpi-fortran-devel
    build:
      skip: mpi == 'nompi'
      string: ${{ module_abi }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_num }}
      variant:
        # scotch_intsize is irrelevant to the ABI marker itself, but keeping it
        # here mirrors the variant matrix of the package being pinned and keeps
        # conda-smithy splitting CI jobs per intsize as before.
        use_keys:
          - module_abi
          - mpi
          - scotch_intsize
        # see note on mumps-seq above
        down_prioritize_variant: ${{ 1 if module_abi == 'ifx' else 0 }}
    requirements:
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mumps-mpi', upper_bound='x.x.x', build=module_abi ~ '_*') }}
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mumps-mpi', upper_bound='x.x.x', build=module_abi ~ '_*') }}
    tests:
      - script:
          - python test-fortran-abi.py mumps-mpi ${{ module_abi }}
        files:
          recipe:
            - test-fortran-abi.py
        requirements:
          run:
            - python
    about:
      summary: Fortran ABI marker for mumps-mpi
      description: |
        Fortran ABI marker for `mumps-mpi`. Depend on this only if you call MUMPS
        from Fortran.

        The C interface (`dmumps_c.h`) is ABI stable across compilers, so C and
        C++ consumers should depend on `mumps-mpi` directly and ignore this
        package.

        The Fortran interface is not: symbol mangling, derived-type layout and
        the Fortran runtime all depend on the compiler that built the library,
        and on Windows both a flang and an Intel ifx build are published.
        Fortran consumers should put the matching ABI in `host:`:

            - mumps-mpi-fortran-devel * flang_*

        The build-string prefix names the ABI: `flang_` or `ifx_` on Windows
        (`flang_` is the conda-forge default), `gfortran_` elsewhere. Depending
        on it run-exports a matching pin, so the ABI you build against is the
        one installed at runtime.

        Nothing enforces this automatically -- pick the prefix matching the
        compiler your recipe builds with. A mismatch still links, and fails at
        runtime.
